title: How to Become a Straight-A Student

questions.q: How long should an ideal study session last, according to Newport?
a: About fifty minutes of intense focus
About twenty minutes with short breaks
About ninety minutes without a break
About two hours with music playing
questions.why: Lesson one says the research he reviewed pointed to roughly fifty minutes as the best length for one focused task.

a: Spending long hours with low focus and interruptions
Studying in short blocks with full attention
Working in a group on a shared project
Reviewing notes right before an exam
questions.why: The summary describes all-nighters and marathon workdays as pseudo-working because concentration keeps breaking.

questions.q: What must you do each night in Newport's work progress journal?
a: Explain why any planned task was not finished
Write down the grade you expect to receive
Plan the next month's assignment schedule
List what you learned in each class
questions.why: Lesson two says the nightly explanation forces you to see the same excuses repeating until they lose their power.

questions.q: What are the three P's of Newport's exam approach?
a: Planning, proceeding and proofreading
Preparing, practicing and performing
Planning, prioritizing and producing
Previewing, pacing and polishing
questions.why: Lesson three names planning, proceeding and proofreading as the steps for working through an exam calmly.

questions.q: What should you do first when an exam begins?
a: Survey the whole paper and plan your order and timing
Start with the hardest question immediately
Write your name and wait for instructions
Answer the shortest question first
questions.why: The planning stage means flipping through the exam, allotting time and choosing an order, with a ten-minute buffer.
